t: This is St Olave's, a small church on the corner of Hart Street and Seething Lane, near Fenchurch Street station. It takes its name from Olaf, the Norwegian king who became Saint Olaf. Samuel Pepys is buried here, the diarist whose detailed accounts of everyday life, the Great Plague and the Fire of London make him a vital source on Stuart London. His wife Elizabeth lies here too. So does Sir John Mennes, a naval colleague Pepys found a poor administrator but a delightful companion. Also buried here are the composer Philip van Wilder and the grocer Monkhouse Davison.
